outcome.technical: plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_floor_guard.py: a new section 'a unit's position, read by pairing' - _layout (each part's non-unit statement indices and each record's slot), _chain, _plan (per level: same depth, same part name, same head token via _own, same pytestmark chain, else not in position), _lcs_rows (one forward LCS table, rows kept one at a time, cut at the last row/column asked), _pairing (tokens mapped to ints; cells inside the common prefix/suffix read off lengths - F=min(i,j) for min(i,j)<=p, F=L-(n-i) at aligned suffix, B symmetric - and only the rest from a forward table on a[p:] and a backward table on the reversed a[:n-s]; equal sequences return None, where in place means the same slot), _in_place (unit: F(i,j)+B(i,j)==L; member: same token and F(k,k')+1+B(k+1,k'+1)==L) and _judge (gathers every cell all pairs ask, one table each way per pair of parts). _compare_definitions and _compare_checks now ask _judge for same-file position (kept pairs, and renames by anonymous dump/signature plus position) instead of comparing the count `place`; `place` stays only in the cross-file move signatures (unchanged rule) and in the finding's words (unchanged text). Rule 5 (same / only added / changed or removed) is still _same_rest/_fit/_added over the same _own tokens: greedy earliest-fit with the recursive fit predicate is exactly 'subsequence at every level' and keeps every existing reason; the pairing tables serve rule 3. Which statements are units, the cross-file rule, reason texts and the block's shape are unchanged. Module docstring, the Python-units section comment and _statements' docstring rewritten for pairing; the closed gap sentence (identical sibling heads keep their position) removed from the docstring and the build guide; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, CHANGELOG.md and plugins/audit/README.md (its floorGuard.mode row stated the count) now state the pairing rule. plugins/audit/reference/execute-task.md states no position rule and is untouched. outcome.descriptive: The floor guard reads a test's position by pairing the statements around it, so a set-up line added above a check no longer calls it moved, while a check moved into a later block whose head reads the same now is.
